**The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** is a strong pick for either appliance: it has a **2,600 W AC inverter** and a **2,073.6 Wh battery**, enough output for a typical single-burner induction cooktop rated up to 1,800 W. [See the product and listing](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2).

For an electric kettle, check its label: its wattage must be **at or below the station’s 2,600 W continuous output**. Battery capacity affects how long you can use it; at full 1,800 W, a roughly 2,000 Wh station lasts about an hour after losses, while a single litre boil is estimated at around 90–110 Wh. [Induction cooktop sizing and runtime](https://powerstationmatch.com/devices/induction-cooktop) · [Kettle energy estimate](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop)
